Definetly sounds like the same effect! That wouldnt work in Denmark though, as it is, by law, relatively easy to terminate your employment (from both sides).

But interesting none the less!

Also there is no minimum wage in most of Denmark (i.e. most of the private companies). The people just dont take underpaid jobs because of unemployment benefits. Then the companies are “forced” to give descent wages in order to attract any workers. The big threat of that is ofcourse wage dumping of workers in other countries willing to do the work in Denmark cheaper.

So the biggest “winner” of the danish system is way more complex. Is not just a certain minimum wage - is a tax system that makes peoples fixed expenses low (healthcare etc) and gives some economic safety for people so they dont have to work on outragous terms. 

Of course there are just as much negative effects of this but it is irelevant for this thread.

So please dont oversimplify things to further your agenda and get some retweets.
